meta.title: Territorial changes and imperial expansion, 1836–1914
meta.scope: Research staging proposal for territorial transfers and changes in effective control. Covers French Indochina, East Asia, Balkans, Russian Central Asia, selected African colonial milestones, United States expansion, Punjab, Burma and British Malaya.
meta.datePrecision: Dates are exact only where primary/official sources support them. Month/year anchors are explicitly flagged in note; entries with unknown day use a non-ISO date string only as research placeholders and must be normalised before engine import.

qualityLegend.verified: Primary treaty, official archive or official institutional record directly supports the legal act/date.
qualityLegend.supported: Credible academic or institutional historical source supports the event; primary instrument/date or boundary details may still need checking.

meta.territorialSemantics: Distinguish de jure sovereignty, occupation, protectorate, indirect rule, administrative reorganisation and effective control. Never convert a protectorate or military occupation into annexation without a separate legal act.
meta.mapSemantics: regionIds are supplied only where an existing 1836 region is clearly identifiable; otherwise [] means no safe crosswalk. Do not infer ownership from modern borders or city names. Existing 1836 regions may be too coarse and require subdivision.
meta.entitySemantics: Entity IDs are research keys and require registry mapping. Some polities are not currently in the 1836 registry or are not sovereign; do not auto-create them as full sovereign entities without review.

events.treatyOrEvent: Capitulation of Algiers

regions.statusNote: Do not transfer all Algeria: the capitulation expressly did not cede sovereignty over the hinterland.

events.note: Military surrender of the capital only. This event is an occupation/control change, not annexation of the entire Regency.

events.treatyOrEvent: Surrender of Emir Abd el-Kader

from.name: Algerian resistance polity under Abd el-Kader

regions.historicalName: Western Algeria / Emirate of Abd el-Kader
regions.statusNote: No exact region IDs: resistance-controlled territory shifted over time.

events.note: Marks the collapse of the principal organised resistance, not a precise legal annexation date for every Algerian territory.

events.treatyOrEvent: Admission of the Republic of Texas to the United States

regions.statusNote: Current map may represent Texas inside a broad US/Mexico border region; requires split.

events.note: Admission date 29 December 1845. The 1844 treaty proposal failed; annexation proceeded by congressional joint resolution.

events.treatyOrEvent: Oregon Treaty

regions.historicalName: Oregon Country south of the 49th parallel
regions.statusNote: Jointly claimed territory; boundary settlement, not conquest.

events.note: Treaty settled the Oregon boundary at the 49th parallel, with Vancouver Island retained by Britain.

events.treatyOrEvent: Treaty of Guadalupe Hidalgo

regions.historicalName: New Mexico and northern frontier territories

events.note: Treaty signed 2 February 1848; Senate ratification and exchange occurred later. Use treaty date for agreement, separate effective date if engine tracks ratification.

events.treatyOrEvent: Gadsden Purchase Treaty

regions.historicalName: Mesilla Valley and Gadsden Purchase strip
regions.statusNote: Southern Arizona and New Mexico border strip.

events.note: Treaty signed 30 December 1853; ratification and payment followed in 1854.

events.treatyOrEvent: Proclamation annexing the Punjab after the Second Anglo-Sikh War

regions.statusNote: The historic Punjab was larger than modern Indian Punjab; boundary crosswalk must include western districts.

events.note: Contemporary proclamation date is 29 March 1849. Do not merge this with the 1846 partial cession/residency arrangement.

events.treatyOrEvent: British annexation of Lower Burma (Pegu)

regions.statusNote: Annexed after Second Anglo-Burmese War; earlier Arakan and Tenasserim cessions occurred in 1826, outside this dataset.

events.note: British India proclaimed annexation of Lower Burma on 20 January 1853.

events.treatyOrEvent: Treaty of Aigun

regions.historicalName: Left bank of the Amur River
regions.statusNote: Cession north of the Amur; Ussuri territory was not yet fully allocated.

events.note: The treaty transferred the left bank of the Amur to Russia; territory between Ussuri and the Pacific remained under joint arrangement pending 1860.

events.treatyOrEvent: Convention of Peking

regions.statusNote: Territory east of the Ussuri to the Pacific transferred to Russia.

events.note: The convention confirmed Russian possession of the territory east of the Ussuri; Vladivostok was founded in 1860.

events.treatyOrEvent: French-Spanish invasion of Tourane (Da Nang)

regions.statusNote: Initial expeditionary occupation; not the transfer of all Annam.

events.note: French forces landed at Tourane in 1858; Saigon was captured in 1859. This is a campaign marker, not an annexation.

events.treatyOrEvent: First Treaty of Saigon

regions.principalCities: Gia Định (Saigon), Biên Hòa, Định Tường
regions.statusNote: Three southern provinces and Côn Sơn; ports and navigation concessions also granted.

events.note: Treaty ceded three provinces, Con Son and strategic concessions. Treaty date is 5 June 1862.

events.treatyOrEvent: Treaty establishing French protection over Cambodia

regions.statusNote: Protectorate: Cambodian monarchy persisted; Siamese and Vietnamese claims and border arrangements continued.

events.note: The treaty established a protectorate, not outright French annexation. Effective control expanded over time.

events.treatyOrEvent: French seizure of the remaining three western Cochinchina provinces

regions.principalCities: Vĩnh Long, An Giang, Hà Tiên
regions.statusNote: Combined with the 1862 cessions, this created French control over all six southern provinces.

events.note: French forces occupied the remaining three provinces in June 1867. Avoid assigning all southern Vietnam to France in 1862.

events.treatyOrEvent: Russian capture of Tashkent

regions.statusNote: Captured 27 June and surrendered 29 June 1865; annexation decree followed in August 1866.

events.note: Separate capture (1865) from formal annexation (1866).

events.treatyOrEvent: Russian imperial annexation of Tashkent and Khujand (decree, month precision)

regions.statusNote: Use month precision: annexation decree is dated August 1866 in the source.

events.note: The event uses 1 August as a month anchor only; exact day is unknown. Keep quality supported and do not treat this as an exact date.

events.treatyOrEvent: Creation of the Governor-Generalship of Turkestan

regions.historicalName: Tashkent, Semirechye and Syr-Darya administrative districts
regions.statusNote: Administrative consolidation; not itself a conquest or a new sovereign state.

events.note: The Governor-Generalship was organised in 1867. The exact date is represented as year/month anchor; avoid using it as a territorial transfer.

events.treatyOrEvent: Defeat of Bukhara and treaty imposing Russian protectorate conditions

to.name: Emirate of Bukhara under Russian protectorate

regions.statusNote: Samarkand and some territory annexed to Russia; Bukhara emirate survived as a protectorate.

events.note: Do not mark the whole Emirate of Bukhara annexed: it survived as a dependent protectorate while Samarkand/Zarafshan were annexed.

events.treatyOrEvent: Treaty of Gandimyan after Russian campaign against Khiva

to.name: Khanate of Khiva under Russian protectorate

regions.historicalName: Amu Darya right-bank and Khivan frontier districts
regions.statusNote: Some territory transferred to Russia; khanate survived as protectorate.

events.note: Khiva was not wholly annexed in 1873; treaty reduced sovereignty and imposed indemnity and foreign-policy constraints.

events.treatyOrEvent: Abolition of the Khanate of Kokand and creation of Fergana Oblast

regions.statusNote: The khanate was abolished and its territory incorporated into Russian Turkestan.

events.note: Unlike Bukhara and Khiva, Kokand was abolished and annexed.

events.treatyOrEvent: Russian capture of Geok Tepe

to.name: Russian military occupation of Transcaspian Turkmen territory

regions.statusNote: Military conquest; not instantaneous control over all Turkmen groups.

events.note: Geok Tepe fell in January 1881; Turkmen resistance and Russian expansion continued beyond the battle.

events.treatyOrEvent: Merv submits to Russian rule (month/day not established)

regions.statusNote: Submission/annexation process; exact date not asserted.

events.note: Date precision is deliberately incomplete; engine import must support year/month precision rather than treating ?? as a real date.

events.treatyOrEvent: Panjdeh incident and Russian occupation

regions.statusNote: Contested frontier between Afghan forces and Russian expansion; not an annexation of all Afghanistan.

events.note: The 1885 clash intensified the Anglo-Russian boundary crisis. Precise final boundary settlement followed later.

events.treatyOrEvent: Treaty of Constantinople recognising the Kingdom of Greece

regions.statusNote: Initial kingdom boundaries were much smaller than modern Greece.

events.note: Recognised Greece as an independent kingdom; the 1832 settlement and subsequent boundary protocols should be distinguished.

events.treatyOrEvent: Union of the Ionian Islands with Greece

regions.statusNote: Cession by Britain to Greece; not a conquest.

events.note: The islands were ceded by Britain and united with Greece in 1864.

events.treatyOrEvent: Convention of Constantinople

regions.statusNote: Boundary adjustment; most of Epirus remained Ottoman.

events.note: Transfer implemented in 1881; do not assign all Epirus to Greece.

events.treatyOrEvent: Treaty of Berlin — recognition of Serbia

regions.historicalName: Serbian principality and newly recognised frontier districts
regions.statusNote: Territory expanded; exact boundary needs historical map crosswalk.

events.note: Treaty recognised Serbia's independence; it was not a new declaration by Serbia in 1878.

events.treatyOrEvent: Treaty of Berlin — recognition of Montenegro

regions.statusNote: Territorial expansion and access to Adriatic; exact boundaries need crosswalk.

events.note: Treaty recognised Montenegro's independence and adjusted its boundaries.

events.treatyOrEvent: Treaty of Berlin — recognition of Romania and Bessarabia/Dobruja settlement

regions.statusNote: Southern Bessarabia was transferred from Romania to Russia; show as separate event.

events.note: Romania's independence was recognised, but the treaty also compelled cession of southern Bessarabia to Russia in exchange for Northern Dobruja.

events.treatyOrEvent: Treaty of Berlin — autonomous tributary Principality of Bulgaria

to.name: Autonomous Principality of Bulgaria under Ottoman suzerainty

regions.statusNote: Eastern Rumelia remained a separate autonomous Ottoman province until union in 1885.

events.note: Bulgaria was autonomous and tributary under Ottoman suzerainty, not fully independent in 1878.

events.treatyOrEvent: Treaty of Berlin Article XXV — Austro-Hungarian occupation and administration of Bosnia-Herzegovina

regions.statusNote: Ottoman sovereignty was not formally extinguished by the 1878 occupation clause.

events.note: Treaty authorises occupation and administration, not immediate annexation. Keep Ottoman de jure sovereignty distinct until 1908.

events.treatyOrEvent: Austria-Hungary annexes Bosnia and Herzegovina

regions.statusNote: Annexation ended the formal Ottoman sovereignty reserved after 1878.

events.note: Date of proclamation of annexation; crisis and international recognition negotiations followed.

events.treatyOrEvent: Albanian Declaration of Independence at Vlora

regions.statusNote: Borders were not yet fixed; neighbouring armies occupied several areas.

events.note: Declaration and provisional government are not equivalent to internationally settled borders.

events.treatyOrEvent: Great Powers recognise Albania as an independent neutral state

regions.historicalName: Albania within boundaries set by London Conference
regions.statusNote: The border settlement left substantial Albanian-inhabited areas outside the new state.

events.note: Recognition on 29 July 1913; borders were determined through separate conference decisions.

events.treatyOrEvent: Treaty of Bucharest after Second Balkan War

to.name: Serbia, Greece and Bulgaria (partition of Ottoman Macedonia)

regions.statusNote: Mainly Serbia
Mainly Greece
Bulgaria

events.note: Treaty of Bucharest was between Balkan allies after the Second Balkan War. The Ottoman Empire's loss of most remaining European territory was settled separately by the Treaty of London (30 May 1913).

events.treatyOrEvent: Treaty of Bardo establishes French protectorate over Tunisia

from.name: Beylik of Tunis under Ottoman suzerainty

regions.statusNote: Bey remained nominal ruler; protectorate, not direct annexation.

events.note: The Treaty of Bardo established French control over Tunisia while preserving the Bey's formal position.

events.treatyOrEvent: British occupation of Egypt after Battle of Tel el-Kebir

regions.statusNote: Formal Khedival/Ottoman status persisted; do not encode as British annexation.

events.note: British occupation began in 1882. The country remained formally under the Khedivate and Ottoman framework until later changes.

events.treatyOrEvent: International recognition of Congo Free State following Berlin Conference

regions.statusNote: Claims and effective control were uneven; not a simple transfer to Belgium in 1885.

events.note: Congo Free State was personally controlled by Leopold II; it was not annexed to Belgium until 1908.

events.treatyOrEvent: German East Africa protectorate claim (charter)

from.name: East African coastal and inland polities

regions.statusNote: Treaty-based claims and effective occupation differed; do not assume complete control on proclamation.

events.note: Date represents imperial protection charter/claim; effective control expanded through subsequent treaties and military campaigns.

events.treatyOrEvent: Treaty of Shimonoseki territorial handover of Taiwan and Penghu
events.note: Treaty signed 17 April 1895; sovereignty handover completed 2 June. Liaodong was also ceded in treaty but retroceded to Qing in November 1895 after Triple Intervention; do not keep it as a durable Japanese transfer.

events.treatyOrEvent: Japan-Korea Protectorate Treaty (Eulsa Treaty)

regions.statusNote: Foreign affairs placed under Japanese control; Korean sovereignty was constrained, not yet formally annexed.

events.note: Protectorate phase precedes annexation in 1910; preserve this intermediate status.

events.treatyOrEvent: Promulgation/effect of Japan-Korea Annexation Treaty

to.name: Empire of Japan / Korea under colonial rule

regions.statusNote: Korea became a Japanese colony; Seoul was the colonial administrative centre.

events.note: Treaty signed 22 August and promulgated 29 August 1910; the latter is used as the effective date per Article VIII.

events.treatyOrEvent: Pangkor Treaty — British Resident in Perak

regions.statusNote: Sultan retained formal position; British Resident's advice was binding in most administration except religion and custom.

events.note: Not outright annexation. The treaty's contested signatories and local resistance should be noted.

events.treatyOrEvent: Pahang accepts British Resident / protection
events.note: British intervention extended to Pahang in 1888; exact instrument date requires primary treaty verification.

events.treatyOrEvent: Formation of Federated Malay States

from.name: Perak, Selangor, Negeri Sembilan and Pahang under British Residents

to.name: Federated Malay States under British paramountcy

regions.historicalName: Perak, Selangor, Negeri Sembilan and Pahang
regions.statusNote: Federation was an administrative union, not a formal annexation of the Malay rulers' states.

events.note: 1896 federation centralised selected administrative functions while Malay rulers remained.

events.treatyOrEvent: British proclamation annexing Upper Burma

regions.statusNote: Annexation proclaimed 1 January 1886; guerrilla resistance continued through the 1890s.

events.note: Do not model the whole country as pacified on annexation day; effective control was contested for years.

events.treatyOrEvent: Newlands Resolution annexing Hawaii

regions.statusNote: Republic of Hawaii consent and Native Hawaiian opposition/petitions must remain in historical notes.

events.note: Joint resolution signed 7 July 1898; transfer ceremony 12 August 1898. This was annexation of an independent republic after the 1893 overthrow.

events.treatyOrEvent: Treaty of Paris ending Spanish-American War
events.note: Spain ceded Puerto Rico and Guam and sold the Philippines for $20 million. Cuba was not ceded to the US: Spain relinquished sovereignty and the US occupied it pending a separate political outcome.

events.treatyOrEvent: Philippine cession under Treaty of Paris

regions.statusNote: Cession treaty followed by Philippine-American War; sovereignty/control was contested and resistance continued.

events.note: Do not model cession as uncontested immediate control over the archipelago.

events.treatyOrEvent: British occupation status reaffirmed (not a second transfer)

regions.statusNote: Context marker only; duplicates military occupation event for clarity in timeline.

events.note: A duplicate process marker is included only if event engines require explicit status onset; omit if deduplicating by date/entity.
